- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per subsequent period to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; apply slight upward bias to avoid premature correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per event to reflect increased volatility and uncertainty.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 (neutral) or low bullishness, model often fails to capture bearish momentum; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid false optimism.
